releases.notes:
### Fixed

- **Lyrics while LRCLIB is down.** LRCLIB, the free lyrics site the mod uses, is down right now, so every song said "Couldn't reach LRCLIB. Offline?". The mod now has a backup: when LRCLIB is down or doesn't have a song, it asks [NetEase Cloud Music](https://music.163.com) instead, a big music service that also has timed lyrics, including for many non-English songs. No account or setup needed. It only takes lyrics from NetEase when the song name matches exactly and the artist or the song length matches too, so you don't get the wrong song's words.
- **No waiting on a broken site.** After LRCLIB fails once, the mod goes straight to the backup for the next two minutes, so songs don't each wait for LRCLIB to time out first.
- **Songs nobody has yet.** If LRCLIB is down and NetEase doesn't have the song either, the mod keeps trying while the song plays, and doesn't remember it as "no lyrics", so it gets them once LRCLIB is back.
- The error line on the **Music** tab now says "Couldn't reach the lyrics sites. Offline?", since there are two now.

releases.notes:
### New

- **Type arrival.** A new choice under **Look → Arrival** for World: each word's letters appear one by one, in reading order, as if someone were typing them into the sky.
- **Galaxy sky.** A new choice under **Look → Night sky**: a spiral galaxy seen at a slant, up and to the left of the lyrics, with a warm core and blue arms dotted with pink. It turns very slowly while the music plays. **Random** can pick it too.
- **Comet sky.** A new choice under **Look → Night sky**: a bright comet low on the right of the lyrics, with a broad warm tail and a thin blue one climbing away from it. Streamers drift slowly out along the blue tail while the music plays. **Random** can pick it too.
- **Antennae.** A new hat under **Look → Hat**: two thin antennae on top of your head with glowing balls on the ends that gently wobble. With **Glow with the lyrics** on, the balls swell and flare with each new line.
- **Flower crown.** A new hat under **Look → Hat**: a leafy vine round the top of your head set with eight small flowers that slowly turn, in your lyrics colour and a paler shade. With **Glow with the lyrics** on, they open a little wider with each new line.
- **Propeller cap.** A new hat under **Look → Hat**: a cap of dark and lyrics-coloured panels with a peak at the front and a little glowing propeller on top. It turns gently all the time, and with **Glow with the lyrics** on it whirls faster as each new line starts.
- **Record card.** A new option under **Display → Record card**: a small card in a corner of the screen with a vinyl record that spins while the song plays, the album cover as its label, the song and artist, and a line with the time played and the time left. Under the record, a thin strip shows the line being sung right now, fading in as each new line starts; a line too long for the strip slides along as it is sung, so you can read its end too (switch it off with **Lyric line** if you only want the song). Pick any of the four corners; on a small screen a bottom card moves up so it never covers your hotbar, and a top right card steps down under your potion effect icons. Its two times always add up to the song length, and when a player doesn't say how long the song is, the card leaves out the empty line.
- **Note crosshair.** A new choice under **Look → Crosshair**: a little music note in your lyrics colour, with its round head on the spot you aim at.
- **Heart and diamond crosshairs.** Two more shapes under **Look → Crosshair**: a small solid heart, and a diamond outline round a dot.
- **Leaving.** A new World setting under **Look**: choose how each sung word goes away. Shrink fades it in place like before, Float lifts it up into the sky, Blow carries it off like a leaf in the wind, back the way the line came so it never crosses the words still being sung, Sink lets it drop down, and Dissolve makes its letters wink out one by one in no set order, like the original mod's fading lines.
- **One big word.** A new World setting under **Look**, on by default: in each line of three or more words, one longer word is drawn clearly bigger than the rest, so every line has a word that stands out.
- **Soft edges.** A new World setting under **Look**: the letters get only their glow, with no dark shadow or outline, for the soft neon look of the original mod. Leave it off if words get hard to read against bright clouds.
- **Neon glow.** The glow round the words, in every layout, is now a deeper shade of the letters' own colour, so pale letters sit in a richer haze like a neon sign. A glow colour you picked yourself is used as before.
- **Each line colour.** A new choice under **Look → Colour**: every new lyric line fades into the next of six neon colours (pink, cyan, lilac, mint, amber and blue). The top bar follows along when its accent is set to the lyrics colour. In World, words that are already fading keep the colour they were sung in, so each line stays its own colour as it drifts away.

releases.notes:
### New

- **Song progress line.** A new switch under **Display → Top bar** draws a thin line under the words that fills up as the song plays. It hides itself when your music player doesn't say how long the song is.

- **Arrival.** A new setting under **Lyrics → Lines** for the World layout picks how each floating word shows up: **Pop** (as before), **Drop** (falls in from above and bounces as it lands), **Zoom** (grows out of nothing) or **Fade** (slowly fades in). The old **Animation** row is hidden in World, since it only ever changed the other layouts.
- **Neon shades.** A new hat under **Look → Hat**: dark sunglasses with rims, a bridge and hinges that glow in your lyrics colour, and a soft streak of light across the lenses. Like the other hats, it flares up with each new line when **Glow with the lyrics** is on.

### Fixed

- **Words stay with their line.** When the sky is crowded, a World word now looks for room only along its own row or the next one, so it no longer drops far below the rest of its line.
- **Words in front of trees.** A World word that would land behind a tree, hill or wall now comes closer and shows in front of it, so you can still read it.
- **Fuller rows.** A flowing World line now fits two or three words on each row, like a little staircase, instead of stacking one word per row. Rows also get wider when you turn up **Size** (but never wider than your screen, so big words don't run off the edge), and a new line no longer gets pushed sideways by words that are already fading out.
- **Softer fade.** Sung World words now fade smoothly into the sky instead of hanging on as dim grey smudges and then blinking out.
- **Lines stay on screen.** A flowing World line that slopes or bows upward now starts low enough that even its highest words, after they drift up while fading, stay well under the top of your screen. New words also no longer get shoved up the sky by older words that are fading out.

releases.notes:
### New

- **Search the settings.** A search box at the top of the settings menu finds any setting by its name, in English or Hebrew. It also knows the choices inside each setting, so typing **halo** or **aurora** finds the setting that has it. Settings that are hidden because of another one, like **Glow colour** while Glow is at zero, still show up at the end, marked **not in use now**. Press **Ctrl+F** to jump to it, and click a result's row to change it right there.
- **Time of day colour.** A new choice under **Look → Colour** tints the lyrics with the sky: warm at sunrise and sunset, pale in the day, lilac at night.
- **Line curve.** A new slider under **Lyrics → Position** sets how much a flowing line slopes and bends. Set it to 0 for straight, level lines like the original mod.

### Fixed

- **Untimed lyrics.** When a song only has lyrics without timing, labels like **[Chorus]** or **[Verse 2]** no longer float in the sky as if they were sung, and blank lines at the top no longer add an empty pause before the first words.

### Better looking

- **Flowing lines over your view.** With flowing lines on, a lyric line now often floats just above your crosshair, like the original mod, instead of always going off to one side. It still keeps the middle of your screen clear.
- **No more words on top of words.** Rows of a flowing line keep apart even on a steep Line curve, an older word that a new one lands on gives way at once instead of showing through it, and a word brought in front of a tree or hill keeps the size and row it was meant to have.

releases.notes:
### New

- **Devil horns.** A new hat: two ridged red horns that curl up from your head, with tips that glow in your lyrics colour. Pick it under **Look → Hat** and see it in third person (F5).
- **Music notes.** Another new hat: three glowing notes in your lyrics colour that circle your head, bobbing and rocking as they go. With **Glow with the lyrics** on, they swell a little on each new line.
- **Spinning cover.** Turn on **Display → Top bar → Spin like a record** and the round album cover in the top bar turns slowly while the song plays, with a small record hole in the middle. It winds down when you pause.

### Better looking

- **Curved lines.** With **Flowing lines** on, each row of World words now bows gently, usually up like an arch, and every word tilts to follow the curve (never more than a gentle lean, even at the ends of a deep bow), like handwriting across the sky. Set **Tilt** to 0 for flat, straight rows.
- **Centred last rows.** When a flowing line runs onto a second row with only a few words left, they sit centred under the row above instead of hugging its left end.
- **Verses stack up.** With **Flowing lines** on, the next lyric line is written just under the one before it, with the same curve, so a verse builds up in the sky like a poem. If you look away, the next line starts fresh where you look.

### Fixed

- **Keep off players** only moves words off players you can actually see. Before, a word could dodge someone invisible or hiding behind a wall and give them away in PvP.
- **Smooth letters with shaders.** With a shader pack on, World words used to fall back to Minecraft's blocky letters, because some packs (like AstraLex) drew the smooth ones as black boxes. The smooth letters are now stored in a way every pack draws correctly, so they stay smooth with shaders too.
